sonnet.problem: The setup says the LORD's words put Him in 'the highest place of honor there is.' That rules out the wrong answers on card 2 (stand guard at My gate, go out ahead of My army) and points to the right one. The text also never calls it a place of honor.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: The card says the LORD swears an oath, 'Not a pinky promise. Not a "we'll see."' Card 11 then asks whether the oath leaves room to change His mind. The card already rules out that wrong answer.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The first sentence repeats the quote 'Rule in the midst of Your enemies.' That was the right answer on card 6, which the baker just answered. Only the last half of the card moves the passage forward.
The wrong answer 'judge' is not false anywhere in the passage. Verse 6 says He will judge the nations, so a baker could argue it fits.
sonnet.rule: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
